settings.title: AI lead scoring
settings.subtitle: Give every contact a score from 0 to 100 that says how likely they are to buy, and see what it costs.
settings.readOnly: You can see these settings but not change them. Ask a workspace admin for the permission lsc.settings.manage.
settings.conflict: Someone else changed these settings first. They were reloaded, so what you see is the saved version. Make your change again.

enable.title: Turn on AI lead scoring
enable.hint: Off until you choose, because facts about your contacts are sent to an AI provider.
enable.label: AI lead scoring
enable.what: When on, an AI model reads a short, anonymous description of a contact and answers with a score and the reasons for it. The score is written to the contact's lead score.

sent.title: What is sent to the AI
sent.deals: How many deals are open, won and lost
sent.activity: How recently the contact was active
sent.engagement: How the contact has engaged lately: counts of its messages, broadcasts opened and links clicked, and how fast it replies (numbers only)

notSent.title: What is never sent
notSent.name: The contact's name
notSent.messagesChat: The text of any message, unless you switch on reading conversations (below)

settings.manualRule: A score a person typed is never overwritten. The AI only fills empty scores and refreshes the ones it wrote itself.

auto.label: Score automatically when contacts change
auto.onBody: A contact is scored when it is created and again when its details change.
auto.offBody: Contacts are scored only when you use the Score with AI button or score the unscored contacts below.

confirm.title: Send anonymised contact facts to an AI provider?
confirm.body: Once on, short descriptions of your contacts (stage, source, tags, deal counts, activity, engagement counts such as messages, opened broadcasts and clicked links, and company name) are sent to an AI provider through OpenRouter. Names, email addresses, phone numbers and message text are never sent. You can turn it off at any time.

banner.platformOff: AI lead scoring is switched off for the whole platform. Nothing is scored, whatever is set here, until the platform operator switches it back on.
banner.noKey: No OpenRouter key is available, so nothing can be scored. Add your own key under AI keys, or ask your platform admin to enable the shared key.
banner.off: AI lead scoring is off for this workspace. Nothing is sent to an AI provider.
banner.ready: Ready. Contacts are scored with {model} using {key}.

backfill.title: Score the contacts you already have
backfill.hint: Queues contacts that have no score yet, up to {limit} at a time. They are scored in the background.
backfill.eligibleNote: Contacts with a score a person typed are left out: the AI never changes those.
backfill.noRight: Your role does not allow scoring contacts. It needs the permission lsc.contacts.score.
backfill.notReady: Turn AI lead scoring on, and make sure a key is available, to score contacts.
backfill.queued: {count, plural, one {# contact is queued} other {# contacts are queued}} and will be scored in the background. Reload the log in a minute to see the results.
backfill.nothingToScore: There are no unscored contacts to queue.

cost.title: Last 30 days
cost.hint: What scoring did and cost over the last 30 days.
cost.averageHint: Total cost divided by contacts scored

payerBy.workspace: Your own OpenRouter key, billed to you by OpenRouter

cost.platformPart: Of the total, on the platform's key

chat.title: Read conversations (pilot)
chat.hint: Off until you choose, because the recent messages of a contact are sent to an AI provider, with personal details partly masked.
chat.label: Read a contact’s conversation when it goes quiet
chat.onBody: About 12 minutes after a contact stops writing, the AI reads the recent messages and notes what the contact is after. It also gives the score.
chat.offBody: Conversations are not read. Scores use contact facts and engagement numbers only.
chat.needsScoring: Switch AI lead scoring on first.
chat.stageBody: When the conversation clearly shows a contact has moved on, the AI picks the next stage. Won and Lost stages are never set by the AI. Choose below whether the change is applied by itself or waits for a person.

masked.title: How personal data is masked
masked.phone: Phone numbers keep only the first and last two digits (+91 ***** ***10)
masked.email: Email addresses keep the first letter and the domain (p***@acme.io)
masked.card: Card, Aadhaar and PAN numbers keep only their first and last characters
masked.name: The contact’s name, and a name someone gives about themselves, keep only the first and last letter

rules.title: What is read, and what is not
rules.quiet: Only chats that have gone quiet, and only the last two weeks
rules.enough: Contacts who only tapped buttons are matched by a phrase table, with no AI call
rules.person: A score or stage a person set is never overwritten
rules.closing: Bots, deleted messages, group chats and automatic replies are left out

confirm.title: Send masked conversations to an AI provider?
confirm.body: Once on, the recent messages of a contact are sent to an AI provider through OpenRouter after the chat goes quiet. Phone numbers, emails, card numbers and names are partly masked first, so what is sent cannot be used to reach the person. You can turn it off at any time.

stageMode.title: How a stage change is made

auto.label: Automatic
auto.body: The contact is moved right away and the chat shows a line with an Undo.

manual.label: Manual
manual.body: The suggestion waits under Stage suggestions until a person accepts or dismisses it.

insight.title: Conversation reading
insight.empty: Not read yet. A chat is read about 12 minutes after the contact stops writing, or you can read it now.
insight.analyzingSlow: Asking the AI. This can take a few seconds.
insight.readOn: Read on {date} from {count, plural, one {# message} other {# messages}}.
insight.privacy: Names, phone numbers and emails in the chat are partly masked before anything is sent to the AI.
